import sys, json, uuid, datetime, hashlib

# The incoming message and this cell's OWN configuration arrive on the same
# stdin document: `params` is one of its three top-level objects, beside
# `envelope` and `body`, and the substrate always sets it ({} when there is
# nothing to hand over). Every knob below is read from it, so
# each one is per-INSTANCE configuration -- two collectors in one colony are
# tuned apart, and a mutation retunes one of them without touching a colony-wide
# environment. The literal beside each name is the shipped default; it is the
# same number the template config and `contract.settings` carry, and a test
# pins the three against each other.
doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
d = doc["body"]
envelope = doc["envelope"]
P = doc.get("params") or {}


def _knob(key, default):
    v = P.get(key, default)
    # A knob explicitly set to null or to whitespace is "not configured", not a
    # crash: an operator who blanks a line in a config means the default.
    return default if v is None else v


def _int(key, default):
    v = _knob(key, default)
    if isinstance(v, str) and not v.strip():
        return default
    return int(v)


def _float(key, default):
    v = _knob(key, default)
    if isinstance(v, str) and not v.strip():
        return default
    return float(v)


def _str(key, default):
    v = _knob(key, default)
    return "" if v is None else str(v)


# --- eviction policy (deterministic, no model judgement) --------------------
WINDOW_TURNS = _int("window_turns", 12)
WINDOW_BYTES = _int("window_bytes", 8000)
TURN_CHARS = _int("turn_chars", 4000)
# The same discipline over the OTHER two legs (GH #91): a tool round and a
# recall bundle enter the same window and would otherwise pass every knob
# above uncapped. A cap here is a bounded PREVIEW -- the full value stays
# addressable in the `round` table, which is the environment this collector
# already owns.
TOOL_CHARS = _int("tool_chars", 4000)
ROUND_BYTES = _int("round_bytes", 16000)
MEMORY_CHARS = _int("memory_chars", 8000)
# --- memory leg ------------------------------------------------------------
# Empty = no memory leg at all (the recall port may simply not be wired). A
# tier ("0"/"1"/"2") turns the leg on and is what the collector asks for.
MEMORY_TIER = _str("memory_tier", "")
# readable | json | both -- which form of the bundle reaches the brain.
MEMORY_FORM = _str("memory_form", "readable")
# --- the memory TOOL (GH #78) -----------------------------------------------
# The leg above is fired BEFORE the model has seen the turn, so nothing in an
# agent can ever DECIDE to ask memory about a time RANGE -- the half of the
# collector issue that did not fall out naturally. The tool closes it: the brain
# emits a `memory_recall` tool_call, the dispatcher routes it by name like any
# other tool, and the cell behind that edge is THIS one. The collector already
# owns the recall port (R-OS-5), so it serves the call itself and hands the
# answer back into its own fan-in -- the round ends where it began (R-OS-2).
# The tier is CONFIGURATION, never a model argument; empty switches the tool off
# and every call is answered with a typed error instead of asked into a void.
MEMORY_CALL_TIER = _str("memory_call_tier", "1")
# --- the seam's own bound (GH #77) ------------------------------------------
# How often a turn may re-enter the brain with a tool round. The round begins
# at the seam, so the seam is what ends it: at the cap the assembled context
# leaves on the answer lane instead of asking again. No dispatcher and no edge
# condition is needed to stop a runaway loop.
MAX_ITER = _int("max_iter", 8)
# --- round robustness (GH #103) ----------------------------------------------
# A round whose fan-in can never complete (a result lost in flight) must not
# park forever. When its last progress -- the newest recorded_at of its rows --
# is older than this window AND the fan-in is incomplete, the NEXT message that
# reaches this cell anyway (the next result, the next turn, a sweep) closes it:
# the missing calls get synthetic error tool_results and the round fires
# through its regular route with hop.round_stale=1. Pure arithmetic, no timer
# of the template's own, no model judgement.
ROUND_IDLE_MS = _int("round_idle_ms", 120000)
# --- pruning policy (GH #76) -------------------------------------------------
# Housekeeping over the two session tables, gated on EVIDENCE: prunable is
# only what a close batch already carried out of this hive (the `batched`
# ledger row written beside the write emission) AND whose delivery is older
# than this gate. Without a ledger row nothing is ever pruned -- rather grow
# than silently lose a turn. Store rows are cell state inside the cell.db,
# not {root} files; the substrate's No-Delete-Policy is about files.
PRUNE_AFTER_MS = _int("prune_after_ms", 604800000)
# --- per-turn episodes (wave 9, track A) -------------------------------------
# Empty = off. Set, and every STORED turn hands the day out a SECOND time, on
# its own route: an episode of a turn then exists at the turn instead of at the
# night close, which is the difference between a question about the last
# exchange being answerable and being answered wrongly.
#
# LLM-free, and deliberately not a second way of saying the same thing: what
# leaves here is the SAME document the close lane hands out, read out of the
# same table in the same order. Whoever decomposes it therefore mints the same
# ids, and the close drain that runs later recognises its own work instead of
# writing a second memory beside it.
TURN_WRITE = _str("turn_write", "")
# --- the curator (wave 11) ----------------------------------------------------
# The caps above bound one ITEM at a time and know nothing about the window they
# are entering. The curator is the missing half: a budget projection that runs at
# EVERY assembly, not at a threshold, and replaces what does not fit with a stub
# that carries its own way back (`thread_recall`). It is deterministic and
# model-free - no condense call, no prose, nothing to drift.
#
# Empty or 0 = curation OFF and this cell behaves exactly as it did before. A
# number is the context window of the configured model, in TOKENS.
CONTEXT_WINDOW = _int("context_window", 0)
# Two marks, not one (MemGPT's shape): at `soft` the curator works, at `hard` it
# reports that it is out of stages. Fractions of the window; conservative on
# purpose - degradation is measured long before a window is full.
CURATE_SOFT = _float("curate_soft", 0.50)
CURATE_HARD = _float("curate_hard", 0.75)
# How many of the newest tool ITERATIONS stay verbatim, whatever the budget says.
KEEP_ROUNDS = _int("keep_rounds", 2)
# What may be elided, DECLARED per tool name and never guessed:
#   env        - the effect is in the environment (file written, row inserted,
#                message sent). The result text is a receipt, not the value.
#   repeatable - a read or a search: running it again produces it again.
#   unique     - not reproducible (a search result, a human's words). NEVER
#                elided, and that is the default for every tool not named here.
# Form: "read_file:repeatable,write_file:env,shell:env" (comma, colon).
RECOVERABILITY = _str("recoverability", "")
# The thread tool: what a stub is worth is what it can bring back. Empty
# switches it off, and a call is then ANSWERED with a typed error rather than
# asked into a void - the same lid the memory tool uses.
THREAD_RECALL = _str("thread_recall", "1")
# The wall against a model that recalls everything back in and eats the saving:
# the share of the window one turn's recalls may spend. Over it, a typed error -
# never a silent truncation, because a silently halved recall is a lie.
THREAD_RECALL_BUDGET = _float("thread_recall_budget", 0.20)

REC_MAP = {}
for _pair in RECOVERABILITY.split(","):
    _name, _, _cls = _pair.partition(":")
    if _name.strip() and _cls.strip() in ("env", "repeatable", "unique"):
        REC_MAP[_name.strip()] = _cls.strip()
# The tool a stub points at is never itself elided: eliding the recovery is the
# thrashing loop every CLI had to retrofit a latch against.
TR_NAME = "thread_recall"
# Store-only markers. They ride in the `turn` json of a round row (the shape the
# `lost` marker of GH #103 established) and are stripped before the wire, so a
# provider never sees a word of this cell's bookkeeping.
PRIVATE = ("lost", "tr", "tp", "_it")

h = envelope.get("header", {})
ctx = h.get("context", {})
hop = h.get("hop", {})
phase = str(ctx.get("col_phase", ""))
lane = str(hop.get("route", ""))
op = hop.get("operation")
rows_affected = int(hop.get("rows_affected", 0) or 0)
session = str(ctx.get("session_id", "") or "default")
turn_id = str(ctx.get("turn_id", "") or "")
# The correlation of one consultation (R-CG-3). It is set on the lane that
# carries an advisor's event back and is what makes the exchange bilateral:
# question and answer travel the SAME lane under the SAME id.
consult = str(ctx.get("consult_id", "") or "")
it = int(ctx.get("iter", 0) or 0)
FMT = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ"
now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime(FMT)
# Progress older than this is stale (GH #103). Fixed-width UTC timestamps
# order lexicographically, so the comparison is a string compare.
IDLE_CUT = (datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
            - datetime.timedelta(milliseconds=ROUND_IDLE_MS)).strftime(FMT)

LANES = ("in_turn", "in_advice", "in_bundle", "in_calls", "in_tool", "in_answer",
         "in_close", "in_prune", "in_round_sweep", "in_memory_call",
         "in_thread_call")
# The bookkeeping turn id of a session close. It belongs to no turn, so the
# row it carries never lands in a turn's slate.
CLOSE_ID = "close-" + session


def boundary_of(ref):
    """The close arrival time riding in a close chain's hop id
    ('close-<session>|<B>'). A ref without one is the pre-#76 shape -- at most
    one in-flight close across an upgrade -- and falls back to now."""
    parts = ref.rsplit("|", 1)
    return parts[1] if len(parts) == 2 and parts[1] else now
# The legs the first assembly of a turn waits for. Derived from configuration,
# never from what happens to arrive: a leg that is switched off must not be
# waited for, and a leg that is on must not be assembled around.
EXPECT = ["leg-window"] + (["leg-memory"] if MEMORY_TIER else [])


def park():
    """Terminal by design: an incomplete fan-in and a lost guard race emit
    NOTHING, exactly like the store-backed tool loop this grew out of."""
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([]))
    sys.exit(0)


def emit(msgs):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(msgs))
    sys.exit(0)


def head(route, ph="", tid=None, extra=None):
    """Every emission carries the full key set the port edges read. A missing
    hop key makes a CEL modifier fail, and a failed modifier SKIPS the edge --
    so keys are always present and empty rather than absent."""
    out = {"route": route, "phase": ph, "turn_id": turn_id if tid is None else tid,
           "session_id": session, "iter": str(it)}
    if extra:
        out.update(extra)
    return out


def store_op(args, ph, tid=None, extra=None):
    return {"header": head("cstore", ph, tid, extra),
            "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": "c-" + ph,
                          "text": json.dumps(args)}]}


def rows_of(doc):
    msgs = doc.get("messages", [])
    if not msgs:
        return []
    try:
        rows = json.loads(msgs[0].get("text", "[]"))
    except Exception:
        return []
    return rows if isinstance(rows, list) else []


def round_select(ph):
    return store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "round",
                     "columns": ["turn_id", "iter", "role", "turn", "fired",
                                 "recorded_at"],
                     "where": {"turn_id": turn_id}}, ph)


def round_sets(rows, iter_):
    """The fan-in state of ONE iteration, read from the slate: the call ids the
    assistant expects, the ids that answered, and the newest write time of the
    round's rows -- its last PROGRESS. A row that cannot be dated still counts
    as progress-less rather than as old: an undatable round is never closed
    (the R-P3 direction -- what the policy cannot date, the policy leaves in
    its pre-#103 behaviour)."""
    expected, received, progress = set(), set(), ""
    for r in rows:
        if int(r.get("iter", 0) or 0) != iter_:
            continue
        role = r.get("role")
        if role not in ("assistant", "tool"):
            continue
        rec = str(r.get("recorded_at") or "")
        if rec > progress:
            progress = rec
        try:
            t = json.loads(r.get("turn") or "null")
        except Exception:
            continue
        if role == "assistant":
            items = t if isinstance(t, list) else [t]
            expected.update(x.get("id", "") for x in items
                            if isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("type") == "tool_call"
                            and x.get("id"))
        else:
            tt = t if isinstance(t, dict) else {}
            if tt.get("id"):
                received.add(tt.get("id"))
    return expected, received, progress


def re_check(r):
    """The scoped re-check of one open round (GH #103): the REGULAR
    round-check, run under the round's own turn, iteration and session -- the
    internal edge promotes all three from the hop. The check itself decides on
    full progress; this only names the round worth asking about."""
    tid = str(r.get("turn_id") or "")
    extra = {"iter": str(int(r.get("iter", 0) or 0))}
    s = str(r.get("session_id") or "")
    if s:
        extra["session_id"] = s
    return store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "round",
                     "columns": ["turn_id", "iter", "role", "turn", "fired",
                                 "recorded_at"],
                     "where": {"turn_id": tid}}, "round-check", tid, extra=extra)


def lost_results(missing):
    """Synthetic error tool_results for calls whose results never arrived
    (GH #103) -- the dispatcher-lid pattern: the tool_call_id is kept, so the
    round becomes fan-in-complete and fires through the REGULAR guard instead
    of through second machinery. The row-level `lost` marker lets the seam say
    hop.round_stale=1; it is store bookkeeping and is stripped from the wire."""
    return [round_insert("tool",
                         {"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": mid,
                          "text": "tool result lost: the round went idle before"
                                  " this call's result arrived",
                          "lost": 1},
                         "round-w") for mid in sorted(missing)]


def round_insert(role, turn, ph, iter_=None, tid=None, rec=None, head_tid=None,
                 fired=0):
    """Every round row carries its session AND its write time: the close lane
    reads a whole session's rounds by the one column, the prune lane cuts by
    the other -- a row it cannot date is a row it will never cut. head_tid
    lets a chain keep its travelling hop id while the row stays under a stable
    bookkeeping id (the close chain does both). `fired` is normally 0 -- a row
    written as ALREADY fired is a round nobody is waiting for (R-CG-3): no
    guard can win it and no sweep can find it open."""
    rid = turn_id if tid is None else tid
    return store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "round",
                     "row": {"turn_id": rid, "session_id": session,
                             "iter": it if iter_ is None else iter_,
                             "role": role, "turn": json.dumps(turn), "fired": fired,
                             "recorded_at": now if rec is None else rec}},
                    ph, rid if head_tid is None else head_tid)


def text_of(doc, origin):
    """The last turn of that origin -- a chat surface delivers one, a batch
    ingress may deliver several and the newest is the one being answered."""
    found = ""
    for m in doc.get("messages", []):
        if m.get("origin") == origin and m.get("type") in ("text", None):
            found = str(m.get("text", "") or "")
    return found


def any_text(doc):
    """The last turn that carries text at all, whatever its origin and type
    say. Two arrivals need this: an EVENT from another agent carries the role
    of ITS conversation, not of this one -- and an ERRAND addressed by tool
    name arrives as a `tool_call` turn whose text is the raw arguments. Both
    times the text IS the message, and a turn written with empty content would
    be a question nobody asked."""
    found = ""
    for m in doc.get("messages", []):
        text = str(m.get("text", "") or "")
        if text:
            found = text
    return found


def window_of(rows):
    """The rolling short-term window. Two cuts, both deterministic:

    the TURN cap already ran in the store (order by id desc, limit N), the BYTE
    cap runs here from the newest turn backwards. Whatever the byte cap cannot
    afford is dropped as a WHOLE turn and everything older with it -- a window
    with a hole in the middle is not a conversation. The newest turn is kept
    unconditionally: the turn being answered is never the one evicted.

    Nothing is deleted. Eviction is a READ-TIME cut over an append-only table;
    the durable record of a conversation belongs to the memory hive, not here.

    `deferred` counts the mid-round turns riding along for the first time
    (GH #103) -- the seam reports them as round_deferred=1 and clears the
    stamp in the same multi-send.
    """
    rows = sorted(rows, key=lambda r: str(r.get("id", "")))
    capped = 1 if len(rows) >= WINDOW_TURNS else 0
    kept, spent, dropped, deferred = [], 0, 0, 0
    for r in reversed(rows):
        content = str(r.get("content") or "")[:TURN_CHARS]
        cost = len(content)
        if kept and spent + cost > WINDOW_BYTES:
            dropped = len(rows) - len(kept)
            break
        kept.append({"role": str(r.get("role") or "user"), "text": content,
                     "consult_id": str(r.get("consult_id") or "")})
        if int(r.get("deferred", 0) or 0) == 1:
            deferred += 1
        spent += cost
    kept.reverse()
    return {"turns": kept, "bytes": spent, "dropped": dropped, "capped": capped,
            "deferred": deferred}


def leg_of(rows, role):
    for r in rows:
        if r.get("role") == role:
            try:
                return json.loads(r.get("turn") or "null")
            except Exception:
                return None
    return None


def cost_of(turn):
    return len(str(turn.get("text", "") or "")) if isinstance(turn, dict) else 0


def thread_of(rows):
    """The tool round in PLAIN order: per iteration the assistant turn that
    asked, then the tool results that answered -- and BOUNDED, because a single
    tool result can be larger than the whole window it is entering (GH #91).

    Two cuts, the same discipline as the conversation window: a per-item
    character cap on tool RESULT texts, then a byte cap over the whole round
    counted from the newest iteration backwards. What the byte cap cannot
    afford falls as a whole ITERATION -- a tool_result whose tool_call was
    dropped is not a round, it is a malformed turn for every provider. Nothing
    is deleted: the full text stays readable in the `round` table.

    A synthetic stand-in (GH #103) travels only while no real result for the
    same call exists: the store keeps both rows, the wire carries one result
    per call id, and the `lost` marker never leaves the store. A stand-in that
    travels in the iteration being fired makes the emission stale.

    Every item is tagged with the iteration it belongs to (`_it`), so the
    curator can spare the newest rounds; the tag is bookkeeping and is stripped
    with the other private markers before anything leaves.

    Returns (items, dropped, capped, stale, names, recalled, tp). The last three
    exist for the curator and for nobody else: the tool NAME behind every call
    id -- the only place a recoverability class can be decided from -- the call
    ids a `thread_recall` already brought back in this turn, and the newest
    provider token count this turn has seen.
    """
    items = [r for r in rows if r.get("role") in ("assistant", "tool")]
    items.sort(key=lambda r: (int(r.get("iter", 0) or 0),
                              0 if r.get("role") == "assistant" else 1))
    groups, capped = [], 0
    names, recalled, tp = {}, set(), 0
    for r in items:
        try:
            t = json.loads(r.get("turn") or "null")
        except Exception:
            continue
        turns = t if isinstance(t, list) else ([] if t is None else [t])
        cut = []
        for x in turns:
            if isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("type") == "tool_call":
                # The tool NAME lives in the provider's `function` object, and
                # that object IS the text of a tool_call turn. Reading it here
                # is the whole of B1: the class of a result is DECLARED per tool
                # and looked up by name, never inferred from the payload.
                if x.get("tp"):
                    try:
                        tp = max(tp, int(x.get("tp") or 0))
                    except Exception:
                        pass
                try:
                    fn = json.loads(x.get("text") or "{}")
                except Exception:
                    fn = {}
                if isinstance(fn, dict):
                    cid, nm = str(x.get("id") or ""), str(fn.get("name", "") or "")
                    if cid and nm:
                        names[cid] = nm
                    if nm == TR_NAME:
                        try:
                            a = json.loads(fn.get("arguments") or "{}")
                        except Exception:
                            a = {}
                        if isinstance(a, dict) and a.get("call_id"):
                            recalled.add(str(a.get("call_id")))
            if isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("type") == "text":
                # An interim answer (R-CG-3) left on the answer lane and the
                # in_answer lane already wrote it into the WINDOW. Repeating it
                # here would show it twice -- and it would stand between an
                # assistant turn and the tool results that answer it, which
                # every provider rejects.
                continue
            if isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("type") == "tool_result":
                text = str(x.get("text", "") or "")
                if len(text) > TOOL_CHARS:
                    x = dict(x, text=text[:TOOL_CHARS])
                    capped = 1
            if isinstance(x, dict):
                x = dict(x, _it=int(r.get("iter", 0) or 0))
            cut.append(x)
        iter_ = int(r.get("iter", 0) or 0)
        if groups and groups[-1][0] == iter_:
            groups[-1][1].extend(cut)
        else:
            groups.append([iter_, list(cut)])
    stale, total = 0, 0
    for iter_, group in groups:
        real = {x.get("id") for x in group
                if isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("type") == "tool_result"
                and not x.get("lost")}
        cut, seen = [], set()
        for x in group:
            if isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("lost"):
                if x.get("id") in real or x.get("id") in seen:
                    continue
                seen.add(x.get("id"))
                if iter_ == it:
                    stale = 1
                x = {k: v for k, v in x.items() if k != "lost"}
            cut.append(x)
        group[:] = cut
        total += len(cut)
    kept, spent = [], 0
    for _, group in reversed(groups):
        cost = sum(cost_of(x) for x in group)
        if kept and spent + cost > ROUND_BYTES:
            capped = 1
            break
        kept[0:0] = group
        spent += cost
    return kept, total - len(kept), capped, stale, names, recalled, tp


def toks(chars):
    """Characters to tokens, as a deliberate LOWER bound. Anthropic changed the
    tokenizer with Claude 4.7+ and the SAME text now yields ~30 % more tokens,
    so `chars/4` is systematically low -- which is the only direction an
    estimate may err in here: a low estimate curates too LATE, never too early,
    and never on a window that did not need it."""
    return chars // 4


def rec_of(x, names):
    """The recoverability class of one tool result. Declared per tool name;
    everything not named is `unique` and is therefore never elided. That default
    is the whole safety property: an undeclared tool costs context, never
    correctness."""
    cid = str(x.get("id") or "")
    if names.get(cid) == TR_NAME:
        # A recall is what a stub points AT. Eliding it is the thrashing loop
        # Claude Code and Gemini CLI both had to retrofit a latch against.
        return "unique"
    return REC_MAP.get(names.get(cid, ""), "unique")


def stub_of(x, cls, names):
    """Restorable compression, Manus' shape: the payload leaves, its key stays.
    The name is a content HASH, so the same payload elided twice reads as the
    same reference (free dedup inside one window), and the line says in plain
    words how to get the original back -- a stub without a way back is just a
    loss with better manners."""
    text = str(x.get("text", "") or "")
    cid = str(x.get("id") or "")
    digest = hashlib.sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12]
    return dict(x, text=("[elided tool_result %s - %d chars - tool=%s - kind=%s"
                         " - sha256:%s - recall: thread_recall(call_id=\"%s\")]"
                         % (cid, len(text), names.get(cid, "?"), cls, digest, cid)))


def args_stub_of(x):
    """Stage 3: the ARGUMENTS of an old call leave, the call itself stays. That
    asymmetry is the point (Anthropic's `clear_tool_inputs: false`): the record
    of WHAT was done is what stops an agent from doing it a second time, and it
    costs almost nothing to keep."""
    try:
        fn = json.loads(x.get("text") or "{}")
    except Exception:
        return x
    if not isinstance(fn, dict):
        return x
    raw = str(fn.get("arguments", "") or "")
    cid = str(x.get("id") or "")
    fn = dict(fn, arguments=("[elided arguments - %d chars - recall:"
                             " thread_recall(call_id=\"%s\")]" % (len(raw), cid)))
    return dict(x, text=json.dumps(fn))


def clean(items):
    """Every private marker off, in one place. `lost`, `tr`, `tp` and `_it` are
    this cell's bookkeeping; a provider never sees a word of it."""
    return [({k: v for k, v in x.items() if k not in PRIVATE}
             if isinstance(x, dict) else x) for x in items]


def curate(msgs, names, recalled, sys_chars, tp):
    """The curator (B3): the window as a BUDGET PROJECTION, rebuilt at every
    assembly rather than folded at a threshold.

    Three properties make it different from every compaction in the field:

    1. **It runs always, not at a cliff.** A procedure that only starts at
       50-90 % fill has to compress very much into very little in ONE step, in
       the hot path, with one attempt and no way back. This one moves small
       pieces every round.
    2. **It costs no model call.** Nothing is paraphrased, so nothing can be
       paraphrased WRONG: the failure class "the fold dropped exactly the detail
       I needed later" cannot occur, because no text is ever rewritten. What
       leaves is a payload whose class says it is recoverable; what stays is
       every word the model may still need to be right.
    3. **Everything it removes leaves a key.** `thread_recall` is the way back,
       and the difference between "condensed" and "lost".

    Stages, cheapest and safest first. After each one the projection is measured
    again and the work stops as soon as it fits -- the curator does the least
    that is enough.

    | stage | what leaves | what stays |
    |---|---|---|
    | 1 | `tool_result` payloads whose class is `env` | the stub, the call, the name |
    | 2 | `tool_result` payloads whose class is `repeatable` | the stub, the call, the name |
    | 3 | `tool_call` ARGUMENTS of old calls | the call and its name |

    Never touched, at any stage or budget: the conversation window (user and
    assistant turns), `system.*`, the tool_call NAMES, the newest KEEP_ROUNDS
    iterations verbatim, and every result whose class is `unique`. That list is
    the prologue protection of the CWL paper, and it is also the reason the
    invariance gate holds: constraints, numbers and time markers live in exactly
    those places, and the curator has no path to them.

    Returns (msgs, report).
    """
    report = {"tokens_window": "0", "tokens_projected": "0",
              "tokens_estimated": "1" if not tp else "0",
              "curate_mark": "none", "curate_stage": "0",
              "curate_elided": "0", "curate_saved": "0"}

    def size():
        return toks(sum(cost_of(m) for m in msgs) + sys_chars)

    before_chars = sum(cost_of(m) for m in msgs)
    window = tp if tp else size()
    report["tokens_window"] = str(window)
    report["tokens_projected"] = str(size())
    if CONTEXT_WINDOW <= 0:
        # Off. The knob is empty, so nothing about this cell moves -- the caps
        # above stay the only bound, exactly as before wave 11.
        return clean(msgs), report
    soft = CONTEXT_WINDOW * CURATE_SOFT
    hard = CONTEXT_WINDOW * CURATE_HARD
    report["curate_mark"] = ("hard" if window >= hard else
                             ("soft" if window >= soft else "none"))
    if window < soft:
        return clean(msgs), report
    # The newest KEEP_ROUNDS iterations are verbatim whatever the budget says
    # (CompactionRL keeps k=2). An iteration without a tag is a conversation
    # turn and was never a candidate.
    floor = it - KEEP_ROUNDS + 1
    elided = 0

    def old(x):
        return isinstance(x, dict) and "_it" in x and int(x.get("_it", 0)) < floor

    for stage in (1, 2, 3):
        if size() < soft:
            break
        report["curate_stage"] = str(stage)
        out = []
        for x in msgs:
            if not old(x):
                out.append(x)
                continue
            if stage in (1, 2) and x.get("type") == "tool_result":
                cls = rec_of(x, names)
                # A call already brought back by `thread_recall` is elided
                # whatever its class says: its payload stands in the window
                # once already, and "one representation per prompt" is what
                # keeps a recall from doubling what it recovered. The stub
                # stays as the ANSWER to its call -- dropping the row outright
                # would leave a tool_call unanswered, which every provider
                # rejects.
                forced = str(x.get("id") or "") in recalled
                want = "env" if stage == 1 else "repeatable"
                if (cls == want or forced) and not str(x.get("text", "")).startswith("[elided"):
                    out.append(stub_of(x, "recalled" if forced else cls, names))
                    elided += 1
                    continue
            if stage == 3 and x.get("type") == "tool_call":
                try:
                    fn = json.loads(x.get("text") or "{}")
                except Exception:
                    fn = {}
                raw = str(fn.get("arguments", "") or "") if isinstance(fn, dict) else ""
                # Only when the arguments are bigger than the stub that would
                # replace them: a cut that costs bytes is not a cut.
                if len(raw) > 200:
                    out.append(args_stub_of(x))
                    elided += 1
                    continue
            out.append(x)
        msgs = out
    report["curate_elided"] = str(elided)
    report["curate_saved"] = str(before_chars - sum(cost_of(m) for m in msgs))
    report["tokens_projected"] = str(size())
    return clean(msgs), report


def cap_text(val):
    """A rendered block enters the window bounded (GH #91), never rewritten.
    The full bundle stays where the memory hive put it."""
    return (val, 0) if len(val) <= MEMORY_CHARS else (val[:MEMORY_CHARS], 1)


def system_of(mem):
    """The memory bundle enters the context window HERE and nowhere else, and
    it enters VERBATIM up to its cap: the collector renders nothing of its own,
    it only chooses which of the two forms the memory hive emitted reaches the
    brain, and how much of it. Returns (system slot, capped)."""
    if not mem:
        return {}, 0
    slot, capped = {}, 0
    if MEMORY_FORM in ("json", "both"):
        for key, val in (mem.get("system") or {}).get("memory", {}).items():
            if isinstance(val, dict) and isinstance(val.get("text"), str):
                text, cut = cap_text(val["text"])
                capped = capped or cut
                val = dict(val, text=text)
            slot[key] = val
    if MEMORY_FORM in ("readable", "both"):
        readable = ""
        for m in mem.get("messages") or []:
            readable = str(m.get("text", "") or "")
        if readable:
            readable, cut = cap_text(readable)
            capped = capped or cut
            slot["recall"] = {"text": readable}
    return ({"memory": slot} if slot else {}), capped


def recall_ask(query, tier, tid=None, call_id="", w_from="", w_to=""):
    """The ONE request shape on the recall port. The ambient leg (once per turn)
    and a tool call (GH #78) travel the SAME edge, so every key is always
    present and empty rather than absent -- a missing hop key makes the
    promoting CEL modifier fail, and a failed modifier SKIPS the edge.

    `memory_call_id` is what tells the two answers apart on the way back: empty
    means the ambient leg of a turn, set means the result of a call.

    The window keys are the first PRODUCER of the recall window the memory hive
    has understood since P15 -- derived at the CONSUMER, out of what the model
    asked for, instead of guessed by somebody upstream who cannot know."""
    return {"header": head("recall", "recall", tid,
                           {"recall_query": query, "memory_tier": tier,
                            "memory_call_id": call_id,
                            "recall_window_from": w_from,
                            "recall_window_to": w_to}),
            "messages": [{"origin": "user", "type": "text", "text": query}]}


def bundle_text(doc):
    """A recall bundle as ONE tool_result text, in the configured form. The
    collector renders nothing of its own here either -- it concatenates what the
    memory hive emitted. The per-item cap (params.tool_chars) runs at READ
    time, like on every other tool result, so the full bundle stays in the
    round table."""
    readable = ""
    for m in doc.get("messages") or []:
        readable = str(m.get("text", "") or "")
    slot = (doc.get("system") or {}).get("memory", {})
    parts = []
    if MEMORY_FORM in ("readable", "both") and readable:
        parts.append(readable)
    if MEMORY_FORM in ("json", "both") and slot:
        parts.append(json.dumps(slot))
    if not parts:
        parts.append(readable or (json.dumps(slot) if slot else
                                  "memory recall returned nothing"))
    return "\n".join(parts)


def memory_result(call_id, text):
    """The answer to a memory_recall call, filed as what it is: a tool result of
    the running round, under the ORIGINAL tool_call_id. Everything after this
    row is the ordinary fan-in -- same phase, same guard, same caps -- so the
    round stays ONE round and memory never learns dispatcher vocabulary."""
    return round_insert("tool", {"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result",
                                 "id": call_id, "text": text}, "round-w")


def thread_result(call_id, text, tid=None):
    """The answer to a `thread_recall` call, filed as what it is: a tool result
    of the running round, under the ORIGINAL tool_call_id. The `tr` marker is
    store bookkeeping -- it is how the next call knows what this turn has
    already spent -- and never reaches the wire."""
    return round_insert("tool", {"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result",
                                 "id": call_id, "text": text, "tr": 1},
                        "round-w", tid=tid, head_tid=tid)


def thread_payload(rows, kind, ref, spent):
    """What a recall hands back: the ORIGINAL rows, out of this turn's own
    slate, UNCAPPED -- that is the entire point, and a recall that re-applies
    the cap it was called to undo is theatre.

    Three ways to name what is wanted, all deterministic and none of them a
    similarity search: a call id (what a stub prints), an iteration number, or a
    plain substring. Nothing here is retrieved by embedding; this is a table
    lookup over rows the cell wrote itself.

    The budget is a WALL, not a cap: over it the call is answered with a typed
    error naming the number, because a recall silently halved is a lie about
    what the model was shown. Returns the text to answer with."""
    cap = (int(CONTEXT_WINDOW * THREAD_RECALL_BUDGET) * 4 if CONTEXT_WINDOW
           else ROUND_BYTES)
    found = []
    for r in rows:
        try:
            t = json.loads(r.get("turn") or "null")
        except Exception:
            continue
        for x in (t if isinstance(t, list) else ([] if t is None else [t])):
            if not isinstance(x, dict) or x.get("tr") or x.get("lost"):
                continue
            text = str(x.get("text", "") or "")
            if kind == "call" and str(x.get("id") or "") != ref:
                continue
            if kind == "round" and str(int(r.get("iter", 0) or 0)) != ref:
                continue
            if kind == "query" and ref.lower() not in text.lower():
                continue
            found.append("[%s iter=%s id=%s]\n%s"
                         % (x.get("type", "?"), r.get("iter", 0),
                            x.get("id", ""), text))
    if not found:
        return "thread recall found nothing for %s=%s in this turn" % (kind, ref)
    payload = "\n\n".join(found)
    if spent + len(payload) > cap:
        return ("thread recall refused: %d characters would exceed this turn's"
                " recall budget of %d (already spent %d). Ask for one call_id"
                " instead of a round or a query."
                % (len(payload), cap, spent))
    return payload


def brain_message(rows, nxt):
    """The ONE seam. Everything the agent LLM is going to see leaves through
    this message and no other: rolling window, memory bundle, tool round.

    It is also where the round ENDS (GH #77). A turn that has spent its
    iteration budget leaves on the ANSWER lane with everything it collected
    instead of asking the brain again, and says so with round_capped=1. The
    round begins at the seam, so nothing downstream is ever needed to stop it.
    """
    spent = it >= MAX_ITER
    win = leg_of(rows, "leg-window") or {"turns": [], "dropped": 0, "capped": 0}
    mem = leg_of(rows, "leg-memory")
    msgs = [{"origin": ("assistant" if t.get("role") == "assistant" else "user"),
             "type": "text", "text": str(t.get("text", "") or "")}
            for t in win.get("turns", [])]
    thread, dropped, capped, stale, names, recalled, tp = thread_of(rows)
    msgs.extend(thread)
    sysm, mem_capped = system_of(mem)
    # The reply half of the bilateral lane (R-CG-3): a model can only pass a
    # correlation id back if it was shown one. The ids of the advice turns
    # STILL IN THE WINDOW travel as data -- no prose, no rendering, and they
    # expire exactly when the window forgets the event they belong to.
    consults = []
    for t in win.get("turns", []):
        cid = str(t.get("consult_id", "") or "")
        if cid and cid not in consults:
            consults.append(cid)
    if consults:
        # The system tree reaches a provider through `text` leaves only, so the
        # ids get one. Three words of label and the raw ids -- the collector
        # still renders nothing, it just makes the data readable where it has
        # to be read.
        sysm = dict(sysm)
        sysm["consult"] = {"open": consults,
                           "text": "open consults: " + ", ".join(consults)}
    # The curator runs LAST and over the finished projection: it is the only
    # thing here that needs to know how large the whole window is, and the whole
    # window is not knowable before every leg has met. `system.*` counts towards
    # the budget and is never a candidate -- what is not in the conversation is
    # not compaction-mortal, which is why hard constraints belong there.
    msgs, cur = curate(msgs, names, recalled,
                       len(json.dumps(sysm)) if sysm else 0, tp)
    out = {"header": head("answer" if spent else "brain", "", extra={
        "iter": str(nxt),
        "window_turns": str(len(win.get("turns", []))),
        "window_dropped": str(win.get("dropped", 0)),
        "window_capped": str(win.get("capped", 0)),
        "round_dropped": str(dropped),
        "round_capped": "1" if (spent or capped) else "0",
        "round_stale": "1" if stale else "0",
        "round_deferred": "1" if win.get("deferred", 0) else "0",
        "memory_capped": str(mem_capped), **cur}),
        "messages": msgs}
    if sysm:
        out["system"] = sysm
    return out


def seam_out(rows, nxt):
    """The seam plus its bookkeeping (GH #103): when deferred turns travel in
    this assembly, their stamp is cleared in the same multi-send --
    round_deferred marks the ARRIVAL at the brain, not every later window that
    still happens to contain the turn."""
    msg = brain_message(rows, nxt)
    out = [msg]
    if msg["header"].get("round_deferred") == "1":
        out.append(store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "turns",
                             "set": {"deferred": 0},
                             "where": {"session_id": session, "deferred": 1}},
                            "defer-clear"))
    return out


def close_batch(rows):
    """The session, handed on in ONE message (R-OS-6).

    The window store IS the durable record of the day; a close request only
    asks for it back. messages[] is the conversation in the order it happened,
    `rounds` carries the raw round rows next to it -- the tool rounds AND the
    eviction report of every turn -- parsed but not summarised and not judged.
    Append-all: what is extracted and what is kept belongs to whoever the
    `write` edge leads to, never to the collector.
    """
    turns, rounds = [], []
    for r in rows:
        if r.get("role") == "leg-close":
            try:
                turns = json.loads(r.get("turn") or "[]") or []
            except Exception:
                turns = []
            continue
        row = dict(r)
        try:
            row["turn"] = json.loads(r.get("turn") or "null")
        except Exception:
            pass
        rounds.append(row)
    msgs = [{"origin": ("assistant" if t.get("role") == "assistant" else "user"),
             "type": "text", "text": str(t.get("text", "") or "")}
            for t in turns]
    return {"header": head("write", "", CLOSE_ID,
                           {"turn_count": str(len(msgs)),
                            "round_count": str(len(rounds))}),
            "messages": msgs, "rounds": rounds}



def day_select(ph):
    """The day so far, in the order it happened. The same read the close lane
    does, and uncapped for the same reason: the knobs above bound a context
    WINDOW, and the index an episode id is minted from counts from the first
    turn of the session -- never from the first turn that still fits in a
    window."""
    return store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "turns",
                     "columns": ["id", "role", "content"],
                     "where": {"session_id": session},
                     "order_by": [{"col": "id", "dir": "asc"}]}, ph)


def turn_batch(rows):
    """The day in the batch form the write path already speaks -- but on route
    `turn_write`, never on `write`. The close route has other consumers (a
    summarizer, an archive); firing it per turn would put a model call on a
    path that is model-free by spec. Same mapping as close_batch, so the two
    lanes hand out the same conversation."""
    msgs = [{"origin": ("assistant" if r.get("role") == "assistant" else "user"),
             "type": "text", "text": str(r.get("content") or "")} for r in rows]
    return {"header": head("turn_write", "", extra={"turn_count": str(len(msgs)),
                                                    "round_count": "0"}),
            "messages": msgs}


# ==================================================================== LANES
# Lanes are read BEFORE phases: a message that arrives over a port edge carries
# whatever col_phase the chain happened to leave in its context, and the lane is
# the only thing that says what it IS.
if lane in ("in_turn", "in_advice"):
    # ONE chain, two occasions. `in_advice` is the return lane of the advisor
    # split (R-CG-3): the advisor's result -- or the question it asks back --
    # arrives long after the turn that asked ended with its interim answer, so
    # it cannot re-enter that round. It is assembled like a TURN and opens a
    # fresh one, which is what makes the follow-up reach the channel in the
    # agent's own voice instead of as a raw advisor reply.
    if op is not None or phase in ("turn-open", "win", "collect", "gate",
                                   "fire-guard", "fire"):
        park()
    advice = lane == "in_advice"
    tid = str(uuid.uuid4())
    # An event carries the role of ITS conversation, so its text is read
    # without one; the row keeps `advice` as its own role, which is neither the
    # user's word nor the agent's own.
    query = any_text(d) if advice else (text_of(d, "user") or any_text(d))
    out = [store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "turns",
                     "row": {"id": now + "-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:8], "session_id": session,
                             "turn_id": tid, "role": "advice" if advice else "user",
                             "content": query, "recorded_at": now, "deferred": 0,
                             "consult_id": consult if advice else ""}}, "turn-w", tid)]
    if MEMORY_TIER:
        # Asked HERE, once per turn, because the collector is the place that
        # decides what enters the context window. The ambient ask carries no
        # call id and no window: it is the free floor under every turn, and the
        # model has not seen the turn yet when it leaves (GH #78).
        out.append(recall_ask(query, MEMORY_TIER, tid))
    emit(out)

if lane == "in_bundle":
    if not turn_id:
        park()
    # ONE port, two meanings, told apart by the correlation key the request
    # carried out (GH #78): a bundle with a call id answers a `memory_recall`
    # tool_call and is therefore a RESULT of the running round; a bundle
    # without one is the ambient leg of the turn.
    call_id = str(ctx.get("memory_call_id", "") or "")
    if call_id:
        emit([memory_result(call_id, bundle_text(d))])
    emit([round_insert("leg-memory", {"system": d.get("system", {}),
                                      "messages": d.get("messages", [])}, "collect", 0)])

if lane == "in_calls":
    if not turn_id:
        park()
    msgs = d.get("messages", [])
    # The async class, as the dispatcher classified it (R-CG-3, delta 2). Those
    # ids are NOT part of the expectation set: they are acknowledged on the
    # spot, under their own tool_call_id, so the assistant turn stays
    # well-formed for every provider. And when nothing else was asked, the row
    # is filed as ALREADY fired -- no guard to win, no open round for a sweep
    # to find, and therefore no idle window racing an advisor's thinking time.
    async_ids = [x for x in str(hop.get("async_calls", "") or "").split(",") if x]
    # The one number in the whole system that is not an estimate: what the
    # PROVIDER counted for the prompt it just answered. It reaches this cell
    # only when nothing in between dropped the key, so it is stored when it is
    # there and never waited for -- a curator that stops working because a
    # provider omitted a usage field is the goose bug (hard-coded 128K), and it
    # fires four times too early.
    try:
        tp = int(hop.get("tokens_prompt") or 0)
    except Exception:
        tp = 0
    if tp:
        msgs = [dict(m, tp=tp) if m.get("type") == "tool_call" else m for m in msgs]
    ids = [str(m.get("id") or "") for m in msgs if m.get("type") == "tool_call"]
    acked = [i for i in ids if i in async_ids]
    waiting = [i for i in ids if i not in async_ids]
    out = [round_insert("assistant", msgs, "round-w",
                        fired=1 if acked and not waiting else 0)]
    out.extend(round_insert("tool",
                            {"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": i,
                             "text": "handed to the async lane: this answer"
                                     " arrives later as its own event"},
                            "round-w") for i in acked)
    emit(out)

if lane == "in_tool":
    if not turn_id:
        park()
    msgs = d.get("messages", [])
    emit([round_insert("tool", msgs[0] if msgs else {}, "round-w")])

if lane == "in_memory_call":
    # The memory tool (GH #78). From the dispatcher's side this is a tool like
    # any other -- it names the tool, an edge knows the cell -- and here the
    # cell is the collector itself, because it is the memory specialist of this
    # hive: it already holds the recall port for the per-turn leg. So the call
    # is served HERE and its answer re-enters the fan-in HERE; the round ends
    # in the collector and the dispatcher only ever routed (R-OS-2).
    if not turn_id:
        park()
    msgs = d.get("messages", [])
    call = msgs[0] if msgs else {}
    # The id comes from the TURN, which is also where the round's expectation
    # set came from -- one source, or the two could disagree and the fan-in
    # would wait for a call nobody can answer.
    call_id = str(call.get("id") or "")
    if not call_id:
        park()
    try:
        args = json.loads(call.get("text") or "{}")
    except Exception:
        args = {}
    if not isinstance(args, dict):
        args = {}
    query = str(args.get("query", "") or "")
    if not MEMORY_CALL_TIER:
        # Switched off. A call that cannot be served is ANSWERED, not parked:
        # asking into a port that is not there would hang the fan-in until the
        # idle exit. Same lid pattern as the dispatcher's budget refusal.
        emit([memory_result(call_id, "memory recall is not configured"
                                     " in this collector")])
    # The window arguments travel as the recall port's own keys. What the model
    # did not name stays empty, and an empty window is a point query -- the
    # memory hive's own default, not a decision taken here.
    emit([recall_ask(query, MEMORY_CALL_TIER, None, call_id,
                     str(args.get("window_from", "") or ""),
                     str(args.get("window_to", "") or ""))])

if lane == "in_thread_call":
    # The thread tool (B5). Same bauform as the memory tool one lane up, and
    # for the same reason: the collector owns the slate a stub points at, so
    # the collector serves the call itself and the round ends where it began
    # (R-OS-2). The difference is the archive -- `memory_recall` asks the hive
    # about the past, `thread_recall` asks THIS TURN's own round table about a
    # payload the curator elided ten minutes ago. Without it every stub is a
    # dead end, and a dead end is worse than no stub at all.
    if not turn_id:
        park()
    msgs = d.get("messages", [])
    call = msgs[0] if msgs else {}
    call_id = str(call.get("id") or "")
    if not call_id:
        park()
    try:
        args = json.loads(call.get("text") or "{}")
    except Exception:
        args = {}
    if not isinstance(args, dict):
        args = {}
    if not THREAD_RECALL:
        emit([thread_result(call_id, "thread recall is not configured"
                                     " in this collector")])
    kind, ref = "call", str(args.get("call_id", "") or "")
    if not ref and str(args.get("round", "") or ""):
        kind, ref = "round", str(args.get("round"))
    if not ref:
        kind, ref = "query", str(args.get("query", "") or "")
    if not ref:
        emit([thread_result(call_id, "thread recall needs one of call_id,"
                                     " round or query")])
    # The chain state rides in the hop id, like the prune chain (GH #76): this
    # script keeps no state between hops, and the internal hive edge promotes
    # nothing but the context keys. The real turn id is the first field and is
    # split back out on the other side.
    emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "round",
                    "columns": ["turn_id", "iter", "role", "turn", "recorded_at"],
                    "where": {"turn_id": turn_id}},
                   "tr-sel", "|".join([turn_id, call_id, kind, ref]))])

if lane == "in_answer":
    if not turn_id:
        park()
    answer = text_of(d, "assistant")
    # An interim answer is an answer -- it enters the window like any other and
    # leaves on the same lane -- but it says so, so a channel can render "one
    # moment" differently from the real reply (R-CG-3).
    mark = {"interim": "1"} if str(hop.get("interim", "")) == "1" else None
    out = [store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "turns",
                     "row": {"id": now + "-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:8], "session_id": session,
                             "turn_id": turn_id, "role": "assistant", "content": answer,
                             "recorded_at": now, "deferred": 0}}, "ans-w"),
           {"header": head("answer", extra=mark), "messages": d.get("messages", [])}]
    emit(out)

if lane == "in_close":
    # The session keeper says a generation is over; the collector answers with
    # the generation. Uncapped by design: the knobs above bound a CONTEXT
    # window, and this is the durable record leaving, not a prompt. The hop id
    # carries the ARRIVAL time as the prune boundary (GH #76): every turn this
    # cell processed before the close is in the batch (one actor, ordered
    # mailbox), every later one is stamped younger and survives a prune.
    emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "turns",
                    "columns": ["id", "session_id", "turn_id", "role", "content",
                                "recorded_at"],
                    "where": {"session_id": session},
                    "order_by": [{"col": "id", "dir": "asc"}]},
                   "close-turns", CLOSE_ID + "|" + now)])

if lane == "in_round_sweep":
    # The re-check occasion a parent tree provides (GH #103): a timer or an
    # operator asks whether any round is stuck. The template never fires this
    # itself -- no schedule of its own, the session-keeper discipline. The
    # question is session-agnostic on purpose: a timer knows no session; the
    # rows carry theirs.
    emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "round",
                    "columns": ["turn_id", "iter", "session_id", "recorded_at"],
                    "where": {"role": "assistant", "fired": 0}}, "sweep")])

if lane == "in_prune":
    # The operator lane of GH #76. The collector never fires this itself; a
    # parent tree wires a timer or an operator to it. The request reads the
    # delivery ledger -- what may fall follows from evidence, never from age
    # alone, and evidence already used (pruned_at) is not asked again.
    cut = (datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
           - datetime.timedelta(milliseconds=PRUNE_AFTER_MS)).strftime(FMT)
    emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "batched",
                    "columns": ["session_id", "batched_at"],
                    "where": {"batched_at": {"lte": cut},
                              "pruned_at": {"is_null": True}}},
                   "prune-ledger")])

if lane in LANES:
    park()

# =================================================================== PHASES
# First assembly of a turn: window leg + optional memory leg, fanned in over
# the round table, fired exactly once by the guarded update. Since GH #103 the
# chain first asks whether a tool round of the session is still open -- an
# assistant row whose guard has not fired -- because a mid-round turn defers
# instead of assembling.
if phase == "turn-w" and op == "insert":
    out = [store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "round",
                     "columns": ["turn_id", "iter", "recorded_at"],
                     "where": {"session_id": session, "role": "assistant",
                               "fired": 0}}, "turn-open")]
    if TURN_WRITE:
        # Next to the machine, never inside it: the round check keeps deciding
        # what happens to this turn, and the per-turn write is a second lane
        # that cannot affect it.
        out.append(day_select("tw-scan"))
    emit(out)

# The other occasion: the answer is a turn of the day like any other, and it is
# the one a question about the last exchange needs. Its insert echo was a dead
# end until this lane existed.
if phase == "ans-w" and op == "insert":
    if not TURN_WRITE:
        park()
    emit([day_select("tw-scan")])

if phase == "tw-scan" and op == "select":
    rows = rows_of(d)
    if not rows:
        # A session without a turn is not an empty batch, it is nothing.
        park()
    emit([turn_batch(rows)])

if phase == "turn-open" and op == "select":
    # Open rounds the policy can date. An undatable open row predates #103 and
    # must neither be closed nor block the session forever: such a session
    # keeps the pre-#103 behaviour and assembles normally.
    open_rounds = [r for r in rows_of(d) if str(r.get("recorded_at") or "")]
    if not open_rounds:
        emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "turns",
                        "columns": ["id", "session_id", "turn_id", "role",
                                    "content", "recorded_at", "deferred",
                                    "consult_id"],
                        "where": {"session_id": session},
                        "order_by": [{"col": "id", "dir": "desc"}],
                        "limit": WINDOW_TURNS}, "win")])
    # Mid-round user turn (GH #103): the turn is in the window already and
    # stays there, but it starts NO second assembly while a round of the
    # session is open -- at most ONE open brain call per session, the
    # telephone model (R-OS-3): you answer when the sentence is finished. The
    # stamp is what the next regular assembly reports as round_deferred=1.
    out = [store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "turns",
                     "set": {"deferred": 1},
                     "where": {"turn_id": turn_id, "role": "user"}},
                    "defer-w", extra={"round_deferred": "1"})]
    for r in open_rounds:
        if str(r.get("recorded_at")) < IDLE_CUT:
            # The parked arrival is itself the next OCCASION: a round whose
            # start lies behind the idle window gets its re-check, and the
            # regular round-check decides on full progress (GH #103).
            out.append(re_check(r))
    emit(out)

if phase == "win" and op == "select":
    emit([round_insert("leg-window", window_of(rows_of(d)), "collect", 0)])

if phase == "collect" and op == "insert":
    emit([round_select("gate")])

if phase == "gate" and op == "select":
    roles = {r.get("role") for r in rows_of(d)}
    if not set(EXPECT) <= roles:
        park()
    emit([store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "round", "set": {"fired": 1},
                    "where": {"turn_id": turn_id, "role": "leg-window", "fired": 0}},
                   "fire-guard")])

if phase == "fire-guard" and op == "update":
    if rows_affected < 1:
        park()
    emit([round_select("fire")])

if phase == "fire" and op == "select":
    emit(seam_out(rows_of(d), 0))

# Tool round: the fan-in of the store-backed tool loop, now re-entering through
# the same seam and therefore carrying the window and the bundle with it.
if phase == "sweep" and op == "select":
    # One re-check per stale open round, all rounds in parallel. Fresh rounds
    # wait, undatable rows keep their pre-#103 behaviour. A sweep that finds
    # nothing stale emits nothing: its observable effect is the round it
    # fires -- this lane is an occasion, not a report lane (the prune lane's
    # heartbeat, R-P5, stays the prune lane's).
    emit([re_check(r) for r in rows_of(d)
          if str(r.get("recorded_at") or "")
          and str(r.get("recorded_at")) < IDLE_CUT])

if phase == "tr-sel" and op == "select":
    # The other half of the thread tool: the slate came back, the answer is
    # written as an ordinary tool result of the running round -- same phase,
    # same guard, same fan-in. The round table never learns tool vocabulary and
    # the tool never learns store vocabulary.
    parts = turn_id.split("|", 3)
    if len(parts) != 4:
        park()
    tid, call_id, kind, ref = parts
    rows = rows_of(d)
    spent = 0
    for r in rows:
        try:
            t = json.loads(r.get("turn") or "null")
        except Exception:
            continue
        for x in (t if isinstance(t, list) else ([] if t is None else [t])):
            if isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("tr"):
                spent += len(str(x.get("text", "") or ""))
    emit([thread_result(call_id, thread_payload(rows, kind, ref, spent), tid)])

if phase == "round-w" and op == "insert":
    emit([round_select("round-check")])

if phase == "round-check" and op == "select":
    expected, received, progress = round_sets(rows_of(d), it)
    missing = expected - received
    if expected and not missing:
        emit([store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "round", "set": {"fired": 1},
                        "where": {"turn_id": turn_id, "iter": it, "role": "assistant",
                                  "fired": 0}}, "round-guard")])
    if expected and missing and progress and progress < IDLE_CUT:
        # The deterministic exit of GH #103: the round went idle with calls
        # still open, and a message reached this cell anyway. The stand-ins
        # complete the fan-in; everything after this is the regular machine.
        emit(lost_results(missing))
    park()

if phase == "round-guard" and op == "update":
    if rows_affected < 1:
        park()
    emit([round_select("round-fire")])

if phase == "round-fire" and op == "select":
    emit(seam_out(rows_of(d), it + 1))

# Session close: the day is read out of the two tables it was written into and
# leaves as one batch. The script keeps no state between hops, so the turns are
# parked as their own leg and meet the round rows again in the same reply.
if phase == "close-turns" and op == "select":
    turns = [{"role": str(r.get("role") or "user"),
              "text": str(r.get("content") or "")} for r in rows_of(d)]
    # Backdated to the close arrival: the parked copy holds the session up to
    # the close, so the next prune takes it along with the day it copies.
    emit([round_insert("leg-close", turns, "close-w", 0, CLOSE_ID,
                       rec=boundary_of(turn_id), head_tid=turn_id)])

if phase == "close-w" and op == "insert":
    emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "round",
                    "columns": ["turn_id", "iter", "role", "turn", "fired",
                                "recorded_at"],
                    "where": {"session_id": session}}, "close-fire", turn_id)])

if phase == "close-fire" and op == "select":
    # The batch and its evidence leave in ONE multi-send: the ledger row says
    # THIS session's day left as a batch at THIS boundary, and it is the one
    # thing the prune lane will ever trust (GH #76).
    emit([close_batch(rows_of(d)),
          store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "batched",
                    "row": {"session_id": session,
                            "batched_at": boundary_of(turn_id)}},
                   "close-ledger", CLOSE_ID)])

# Prune (GH #76): one chain of two deletes per batched-and-aged session, all
# sessions in parallel. The chain state (boundary, then the turn count) rides
# in the hop id -- the script keeps no state between hops -- and the report is
# the rows_affected of the deletes themselves, never a re-read of what fell.
if phase == "prune-ledger" and op == "select":
    newest = {}
    for r in rows_of(d):
        s = str(r.get("session_id") or "")
        b = str(r.get("batched_at") or "")
        if s and b and b > newest.get(s, ""):
            newest[s] = b
    if not newest:
        # No evidence, no cut -- and an answer anyway: the operator lane asked.
        emit([{"header": head("prune", "", extra={"session_id": "",
                                                  "pruned_turns": "0",
                                                  "pruned_rounds": "0",
                                                  "prune_boundary": ""}),
               "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "text",
                             "text": "pruned nothing: no batched session behind the age gate"}]}])
    emit([store_op({"operation": "delete", "table": "turns",
                    "where": {"session_id": s, "recorded_at": {"lte": b}}},
                   "prune-t", "prune|" + b, extra={"session_id": s})
          for s, b in newest.items()])

if phase == "prune-t" and op == "delete":
    parts = turn_id.split("|")
    if len(parts) != 2 or not parts[1]:
        park()
    emit([store_op({"operation": "delete", "table": "round",
                    "where": {"session_id": session,
                              "recorded_at": {"lte": parts[1]}}},
                   "prune-r", turn_id + "|" + str(rows_affected))])

if phase == "prune-r" and op == "delete":
    parts = turn_id.split("|")
    if len(parts) != 3 or not parts[1]:
        park()
    emit([store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "batched",
                    "set": {"pruned_at": now},
                    "where": {"session_id": session,
                              "batched_at": {"lte": parts[1]}}},
                   "prune-mark", turn_id),
          {"header": head("prune", "", extra={"pruned_turns": parts[2],
                                              "pruned_rounds": str(rows_affected),
                                              "prune_boundary": parts[1]}),
           "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "text",
                         "text": "pruned session %s: %s turns, %s rounds up to %s"
                                 % (session, parts[2], rows_affected, parts[1])}]}])

park()

window_turns.description: Rolling window: how many of the newest turns of the session enter the context. The cut runs in the store as order by id desc + limit.

window_bytes.description: Rolling window: byte cap over the turn texts. Counted from the newest turn backwards; whole turns are dropped, never truncated, and the newest turn is kept even when it alone exceeds the cap.

turn_chars.description: Per-turn character cap applied before the byte cap. A single pathological turn cannot eat the whole window.

tool_chars.description: Per-item character cap on tool RESULT texts before they enter the seam. A single large tool result would otherwise flood the context window past every window knob; the full text stays readable in the round table.

round_bytes.description: Byte cap over the whole tool round. Counted from the newest iteration backwards; what does not fit falls as a WHOLE iteration, because a tool_result whose tool_call was dropped is a malformed turn for every provider.

memory_chars.description: Character cap on the memory bundle as it enters system.memory. Applies to the readable block and to every {text} leaf of the machine-readable form.

max_iter.description: How many times a turn may re-enter the brain with a tool round. At the cap the seam leaves through the answer lane with hop.round_capped=1 instead of asking again - the seam opened the round, so the seam closes it.

round_idle_ms.description: Idle window of one tool round in milliseconds (default two minutes). A round whose last progress - the newest recorded_at of its rows - lies behind this window while its fan-in is still incomplete is closed at the NEXT message that reaches the cell anyway (the next result, the next turn, an in_round_sweep request): the missing calls get synthetic error tool_results with their tool_call_id kept, then the round fires through its regular route with hop.round_stale=1. Pure arithmetic, no timer of the template's own.

memory_tier.description: Memory leg. Empty = no memory leg: the recall port is not wired and the assembly waits for the window leg alone. '0' / '1' / '2' request that recall tier once per turn.

memory_call_tier.description: Recall tier of the memory TOOL (GH #78). The brain asks for memory itself with a `memory_recall` tool_call; the dispatcher routes it by name, and the cell behind that edge is the collector, which serves the call on the same recall port the per-turn leg uses and answers it with a tool_result under the original tool_call_id. The tier is configuration, never a model argument. Empty switches the tool off: every call is then answered with a typed error result instead of being asked into a void.

memory_form.description: Which form of the bundle reaches the brain: 'readable' the rendered block a model reads, 'json' the machine-readable bundle, 'both'. The collector renders nothing of its own; both forms come from the memory hive verbatim.

prune_after_ms.description: Age gate on the prune lane in milliseconds (default seven days). A session is pruned only when its close batch left the collector (the 'batched' ledger row is the evidence) AND that delivery is older than this gate. Without a ledger row nothing is ever pruned.

turn_write.description: Per-turn episodes. Empty = off, and nothing about the collector moves. Set, and every stored turn - the inbound one and the answer - hands the whole session out again on route 'turn_write': the same document the close lane produces on route 'write', read out of the same table in the same order, so whoever decomposes it mints the same episode ids and the close drain that follows recognises its own work. Model-free. Wire it to the SAME batch entry the write route feeds; leave it off when no such consumer exists, or every turn emits a route nobody routes.

context_window.description: The curator's budget: the context window of the configured model, in TOKENS. 0 or empty = curation OFF and the cell behaves exactly as it did before wave 11 - the per-item caps stay the only bound. Set it, and every assembly is projected against the budget and elides what does not fit, deterministically and without a model call.

curate_soft.description: The working mark, as a fraction of context_window. At or above it the curator elides in stages until the projection fits under it again. Conservative on purpose: retrieval degradation is measured long before a window is actually full.

curate_hard.description: The emergency mark, as a fraction of context_window. It changes no behaviour of its own - it is REPORTED as hop.curate_mark='hard' and means: the curator has run out of stages and the next thing that could give is prose. That is the signal a fold lane subscribes to.

keep_rounds.description: How many of the NEWEST tool iterations stay verbatim whatever the budget says. A curator that elides what the model is holding in its hands right now does not save context, it causes a retry.

recoverability.description: What may be elided, DECLARED per tool name and never guessed. Form: 'read_file:repeatable,write_file:env'. env = the effect is already in the environment and the result text is a receipt; repeatable = a read or a search that running again reproduces; unique = not reproducible, and the DEFAULT for every tool not named here. An undeclared tool therefore costs context, never correctness.

thread_recall.description: The thread tool: the model asks for an elided payload back by call id, round or substring, and the collector serves the call itself out of its own round table - the same bauform as the memory tool. Empty switches it off, and a call is then answered with a typed error instead of being asked into a void. A stub without a way back is worse than no stub at all, so switching this off should mean switching curation off.

thread_recall_budget.description: The share of context_window one turn's recalls may spend. Over it the call is REFUSED with a typed error naming the number - never truncated, because a silently halved recall is a lie about what the model was shown. Without a context_window the round byte cap stands in as the wall.

description.purpose: The context orchestrator of one agent: it decides what enters the LLM's context window and what leaves it. Rolling short-term turns of the session (user AND assistant, so a conversation can reference its own previous turns without retrieval), the memory bundle, the tool round, and a deterministic eviction policy over all three of them. Everything the brain sees leaves through ONE message on route 'brain' - and when the round has spent its iteration budget, that same seam leaves on 'answer' instead, so a runaway loop ends where it began. A round that lost a result does not park forever: when its last progress lies behind params.round_idle_ms, the next message that reaches the cell closes it - the missing calls get synthetic error tool_results with their tool_call_id kept, and the round fires through its regular route with hop.round_stale=1. A user turn arriving while a round of its session is open is written into the window but starts NO second assembly: it rides with the next regular assembly (hop.round_deferred=1 on that arrival) - at most one open brain call per session. On a close request the collector reads its own store back and hands the whole session on as one batch on route 'write', and writes the delivery into the 'batched' ledger in the same multi-send. On a prune request it cuts the rows of sessions that ledger names as delivered-and-aged, and reports the cut on route 'prune'. A tool the dispatcher classified as ASYNC (hop.async_calls) opens no fan-in expectation at all: it is acknowledged on the spot under its own tool_call_id, and a bundle that asked for nothing else is filed as already fired - the turn ends with the interim answer instead of racing an idle window against thinking time. Its result comes back later on the in_advice lane as an EVENT with a consult_id, is assembled like a turn and opens a FRESH round, so the follow-up reaches the channel in the agent's own voice; the ids of the advice turns still in the window travel to the brain as system.consult.open, which is how a reply finds its way back to the right open question. Since 1.1.0 the assembly is also CURATED: before it leaves, the finished projection is measured against params.context_window and, over the soft mark, tool payloads whose recoverability is DECLARED are replaced in stages by stubs carrying a content hash and a thread_recall key - LLM-free, at every round rather than at a threshold, and never touching the conversation, system.*, a tool_call NAME or the newest params.keep_rounds iterations. Because no text is ever rewritten, the same question has the same answer basis before and after any number of curations.
description.use_when: Between an agent's inbound surface and its LLM, in place of a persona cell that only injects a system prompt and a prep cell that only mints a turn id. Wire the ten entry lanes and the five exit routes in the SAME mutation that instantiates the hive.
description.not_in_scope: No inference and no persona (identity is not context assembly, and the brain edge is ONE seam so an agent split can happen behind it later without re-cutting the collector). No tool fan-OUT: routing a tool_call to the right tool is a dispatcher's job, the collector only fans the results back in. No judgement about memory: the collector READS the recall bundle and it hands the closed session on unfiltered, but what is extracted and what is kept belongs to the receiver of the write batch. Eviction is deterministic policy, never a model judgement, and no CAP deletes: every cap is a read-time cut, the full value stays addressable in the round store. Rows fall only on the in_prune lane, only with delivery evidence in the batched ledger and behind the age gate - and the collector never fires that lane itself: no schedule, no self-initiated housekeeping, the parent tree decides whether a timer is wired to it. No timer and no schedule of the template's own anywhere: the in_round_sweep lane is an OCCASION a parent tree may provide, and a sweep that finds nothing stale emits nothing. No classification of the async class: the dispatcher declares it and this cell obeys the marker. No rendering of an advisor event: what arrives on in_advice enters the window as its text, and the correlation ids leave as raw data. No curation of the conversation and no prose: the curator elides declared-recoverable tool payloads and nothing else, it asks no model, and it removes no row - a stub answers its tool_call exactly like the payload did. What is not declared is unique and is never touched, so an undeclared tool costs context and never correctness. No fold: turning a round into prose is a lane this cell does not have.
description.emits_meaning: route cstore: store ops of the current step (hop.phase carries the state, hop.turn_id correlates the turn; both are promoted to context by the edge). route recall: the memory requests of this hive - one ambient request per turn (hop.memory_call_id empty) and one per memory_recall tool call (hop.memory_call_id = the tool_call_id, hop.recall_window_from / recall_window_to = the time range the MODEL asked for, GH #78). Both travel the same edge, so every key is always present and empty rather than absent. route brain: THE assembled context window - system carries the memory bundle and, when advice turns are still in the window, system.consult.open with their raw correlation ids, messages[] the rolling window followed by the tool round, hop.iter the loop counter for the next call, hop.window_turns / window_dropped / window_capped and hop.round_dropped / round_capped / memory_capped what the caps did, hop.round_stale=1 when the round was closed by the idle exit (a synthetic result travels in place of each lost one; a late real result wins over its stand-in), hop.round_deferred=1 when a deferred mid-round turn rides in this window for the first time (the stamp is cleared in the same multi-send). route answer: the brain's final turn on its way out after it has been written into the window - OR, with hop.round_capped=1, the assembled context of a round that reached params.max_iter and will not ask again. route write: one batch per closed session, messages[] the whole conversation in order, the raw round rows in the top-level slot 'rounds', hop.turn_count / round_count their sizes. route prune: one report per pruned session - hop.session_id, hop.pruned_turns, hop.pruned_rounds, hop.prune_boundary - or a single zero report when no session was eligible; the deletes themselves never leave the hive. An incomplete fan-in and a lost guard race emit NOTHING (empty multi-send, terminal by design).
